主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) charged the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and its affiliate for systemic regulatory and compliance failures. The charges included a failure to enforce or fully understand rules to prevent abusive short selling. CBOE agreed to pay a $6 million penalty and implement major remedial measures to settle the SEC's charges. This penalty marks the first financial penalty assessed against an exchange for violations related to its regulatory oversight. The SEC investigation found that CBOE failed to adequately police and control conflicts between self-regulatory obligations and the business interests of its member firms. CBOE's surveillance program was ineffective, failing to detect wrongdoing despite numerous red flags. The SEC emphasized the importance of SROs in enforcing securities laws and regulating member firms. CBOE's failures included a lack of formal training for investigators and an inadequate understanding of Reg. SHO. The SEC's order highlighted that CBOE moved Reg. SHO compliance responsibilities in 2008, which negatively impacted its enforcement program. CBOE did not take action against any firm for Reg. SHO violations after the transfer. The SEC also noted that CBOE staff were confused about whether Reg. SHO applied to retail customers and failed to properly investigate potential violations. The SEC also charged CBOE for regulatory failures, including failing to provide requested information to SEC staff and assisting a member firm during an SEC investigation. CBOE also edited the firm's draft submission, which contained inaccurate and misleading information. The SEC's order found that CBOE violated several sections of the Securities Exchange Act, including Section 19(b)(1) and Section 19(g)(1), as well as Section 17(a) and Rule 17a-1, for failing to promptly provide information related to the member firm under SEC investigation. CBOE and its affiliate, C2 Options Exchange, agreed to settle the charges without admitting or denying the findings. CBOE agreed to pay $6 million, accept a censure, and cease-and-desist order, along with implementing significant undertakings. C2 also agreed to a censure and cease-and-desist order. CBOE reorganized its Regulatory Services Division, hired a chief compliance officer, and updated its policies and procedures. The SEC took into account CBOE's remedial efforts in reaching the settlement and decided not to impose limitations on CBOE's activities under Section 19(h)(1) of the Exchange Act.
